Hi all — jumping in with technical clarifications before the deep-dive: 

1) Hosted API (standard):
   - Routing: requests land in the nearest region endpoint but we have optional region pins to prefer eu-west endpoints. However, Hosted has automated fallback policies: if eu-west capacity is exhausted and policy allows, traffic may be routed temporarily to a compatible region. That fallback can be disabled per-customer in many cases but with impacts to availability under peak load.
   - Storage: We provide EU-only storage options for model KV caches and logs when tenant is pinned to EU; we can also disable long-term KV persistence.

2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in eu-west):
   - Provides isolated capacity with predictable throughput and no automated cross-region fallback unless explicitly configured. Good middle ground for predictable performance and region control.

3) Private deployment (VPC / on-prem):
   - Full control: networking and storage remain within customer-managed VPC or on-prem. Best fit for strict legal requirements that prohibit any third-party storage outside EU.

Suggested pilot path for NovaBank: start with a Dedicated pool pinned to eu-west with VPC peering for control over network egress. If legal sign-off demands, transition to Private VPC or on-prem in a later phase.
